Before I show you the full checklist, I need two quick facts:

**Is your business already registered with CAC** (the Corporate Affairs Commission)? That is, do you have a registered business name or company?

Perfect. Here's your checklist in order. The steps follow the regulators' own rules, so you'll need to do them in this sequence to avoid delays.

**Start here — before you make anything**

1. **Check your product meets NAFDAC's fruit juice rules** [1] — NAFDAC has specific requirements for zobo drinks. Make sure your recipe and ingredients comply before you go further. This is a one-time check.

2. **Get food handler medical tests for your production staff** [1] — Anyone making the drink needs a medical certificate. This is required before NAFDAC will inspect your facility, and you'll need to renew it regularly.

**Register your business**

3. **CAC business name registration** [2] — As a sole proprietor, you'll register a business name with the Corporate Affairs Commission. This is your foundation; most other steps depend on it.

4. **Search for your trademark** [3] — Before you file for trademark protection, check that your brand name isn't already taken. This is quick and inexpensive.

5. **Federal Tax ID** [6] — Once CAC approves your business name, apply for your Tax ID number with the Nigeria Revenue Service. You'll need this for NAFDAC and other registrations.

6. **Oyo State tax registration** [6] — Register with the Oyo State Internal Revenue Service as well.

**Get your facility ready**

7. **Make sure your production facility meets NAFDAC standards** [1] — Your kitchen or workshop must have proper hygiene, equipment and layout. NAFDAC will inspect this, so get it right before you apply.

8. **Apply for NAFDAC facility inspection** [1] — Once your facility is ready and you have your Tax ID, ask NAFDAC to inspect it. They'll check your equipment, hygiene, storage and processes.

**Protect your brand**

9. **File your trademark application** [3] — After the search, file to register your brand name.

10. **Trademark examination and acceptance** [3] — NAFDAC reviews your application.

11. **Trademark publication and opposition period** [3] — Your trademark is published; others have time to object.

12. **Get your trademark registration certificate** [3] — Once opposition ends, you receive your certificate.

**Register your product with NAFDAC**

13. **Laboratory analysis of your drink samples** [1] — NAFDAC tests your zobo to confirm it meets the fruit juice regulations. This happens after your facility inspection.

14. **NAFDAC product registration** [1] — Once the lab confirms your product is safe, NAFDAC registers it. This is what allows you to legally sell.

15. **Product labelling approval** [1] — Your labels must show all required information. NAFDAC approves them before you print.

**Register your premises with Oyo State**

16. **Oyo State business premises registration** [7] — Register your production location with the Oyo State Ministry of Trade, Industry, Investment and Cooperatives. You'll need your CAC registration and state tax registration first.

**Ongoing**

After you start, you'll need to renew your CAC registration annually, renew your NAFDAC product registration every few years, and renew your state premises registration yearly.

Would you like me to go through any of these steps in more detail, or do you have questions about fees, documents or timelines?

2. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)
3. Trademark registration — Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry (Nigerian Intellectual Property Office) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nipo.gov.ng](https://nipo.gov.ng/trademark.jsp)
4. Data protection requirements for businesses that collect customers' personal data — Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [ndpc.gov.ng](https://ndpc.gov.ng/dpco-registration-requirements/)
5. Product certification for locally made products — Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) MANCAP (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [son.gov.ng](https://son.gov.ng/mancapservice/)
6. Tax registration — federal (Nigeria Revenue Service) and state internal revenue services (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [www.nrs.gov.ng](https://www.nrs.gov.ng/)

CAC business name registration costs **₦10,000** and takes **24 working hours** [1]. That fee includes certified copies of your registration documents.

Before you register, you'll also need to reserve your business name, which costs ₦500 per name and takes about 4 working hours [1]. The name reservation is valid for 60 days, so you need to complete the full registration within that time.

You'll do everything online through the CAC's Company Registration Portal at https://icrp.cac.gov.ng/ [1]. The whole process is straightforward: search for name availability, reserve it, fill in form CAC-BN with your details and documents, pay online, and download your certificate.

Please confirm these fees with CAC before you pay, as they can change at any time.

**Sources**

1. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) — Business name registration — sole proprietorship (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)

NAFDAC won't register your product until they've inspected your facility and confirmed it meets their standards. Here's why: when you apply for product registration, NAFDAC's approval team reviews your documents, checks the results of their GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice) inspection of your facility, and looks at your product's laboratory test reports. They only move your application forward to their approval meeting once all of that is satisfactory [1].

In other words, the facility inspection is how NAFDAC verifies that you can actually make the drink safely and consistently. Without that proof, they have no basis to approve your specific product. So the inspection has to come first.

1. NAFDAC requirements for packaged fruit drinks made in Nigeria — NAFDAC product registration (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nafdac.gov.ng](https://nafdac.gov.ng/food/guideline-for-micro-scale-enterprises/)

Alright, here's your full checklist for opening the pharmacy. The order matters because some things depend on others—the regulators set it up that way.

**Start here (you can do these now)**

1. Make sure your premises meet PCN standards [1] — the building, layout and equipment must fit what the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria requires for a pharmacy.

2. Register your business name with CAC as a partnership [2] — this is your foundation. Once you have this, most other registrations can follow.

3. Search for trademark availability (optional but smart) [3] — if you want to protect your pharmacy's name or logo, check if it's free first.

**Once CAC registration comes through**

4. Publish your privacy policy and notices [4] — because you're collecting customer names and phone numbers, you must tell them how you'll use their data.

5. Set up lawful basis and get customer consent [4] — you need a proper reason to collect their data and their permission.

6. Set up data security and breach reporting [4] — you must protect their information and know what to do if something goes wrong.

7. Check that your ownership structure meets PCN rules [1] — the Pharmacy Council needs to approve that a partnership of pharmacists is allowed.

8. Get your Federal Tax ID [5] — you'll need this for all tax matters.

9. Register with Lagos State tax authority [5] — separate from federal tax.

10. Register your premises with Lagos State [6] — the state needs to know where you're operating.

**Before you can open**

11. Check if your business counts as "major importance" for data protection [4] — this decides if you need extra data protection steps.

12. File your trademark application if you're protecting your name [3] — only if you did the search first.

13. Get PCN location approval [1] — they approve your specific location.

14. Appoint a Data Protection Officer if needed [4] — only if step 11 says you qualify.

15. Get VAT registration if your business grows [5] — only when you're no longer a small business.

16. Complete trademark examination [3] — if you filed one.

17. Get PCN premises registration with inspection [1] — they inspect your actual pharmacy before you open.

18. Wait for trademark publication and opposition period [3] — if you filed one.

19. Display your certificates and meet operating standards [1] — final setup before opening.

20. Get your trademark registration certificate [3] — if you filed one.

**Every year**

21. Keep your superintendent pharmacist licensed [1] — at least one of you must stay registered and licensed with PCN.

22. File CAC annual returns [2] — every year.

23. Renew your Lagos State premises registration [6] — every year.

24. Register with NDPC if you're major importance [4] — only if step 11 says you qualify.

25. Do NDPC compliance audits [4] — only if you're registered as major importance.

26. Renew your PCN premises registration [1] — every year.

27. Renew your trademark if you registered one [3] — every 10 years.

The key thing to start with is getting your premises right and your CAC registration done. Once CAC approves you, everything else can move forward. Want me to go deeper into any of these steps?

**Start here — you can do these right away:**

2. **Search for trademark availability** [2] — Before you invest in branding, check that your product name isn't already registered by someone else.

3. **Get food handler medical tests for your production staff** [1] — Anyone making your drink needs a medical certificate. This is required and can be done now.

5. **Register for a Federal Tax ID** [4] — You'll need this before you can apply for the NAFDAC facility inspection.

6. **Register with Oyo State tax** [4] — After your federal tax ID, register with Oyo State Internal Revenue Service.
